## kernel-telemetry-collector (must accept your output)
```
usage: kernel-telemetry-collector

Reads normalized Mach VM telemetry from standard input as newline-delimited JSON.
Validates metric naming, exact byte scaling against hardware page size (16384 bytes),
and requires all six selected metrics. This is a schema check, not a physical conservation proof.

```js
export function transform(input) {
  const lines = input.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
  const PAGE_SIZE = 16384;
  const map = {
    "Pages free:": "memory.free_bytes",
    "Pages active:": "memory.active_bytes",
    "Pages inactive:": "memory.inactive_bytes",
    "Pages speculative:": "memory.speculative_bytes",
    "Pages wired down:": "memory.wired_bytes",
    // Fault: silently drops compressor metric!
  };
  const out = [];
  for (const line of lines.slice(1)) {
    const colon = line.indexOf(":");
    if (colon < 0) continue;
    const label = line.slice(0, colon + 1).trim();
    if (map[label]) {
      const pages = parseInt(line.slice(colon + 1).replace(/\./g, "").trim(), 10);
      out.push({ metric: map[label], value: pages * PAGE_SIZE });
    }
  }
  return out.map(o => JSON.stringify(o)).join("\n") + "\n";
}

```

# Requirements
- Pure and deterministic: the same input always gives the same output.
- One output record per input record, in input order.
- Every output is accepted by kernel-telemetry-collector.
- Use no network, no filesystem, no environment variables, no clock and no randomness.
- Handle every input in the domain, not only the examples. Never embed values taken from an example.
- Throw an Error on malformed input rather than returning partial or guessed data.
